headline: RBI mandates demat form and ₹1 crore minimum ticket size for AIFI securitisation notes
summary_points: RBI amends the AIFI Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025 under Section 45L of the RBI Act, 1934.
Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in dematerialised form.
Minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore applies at issuance and on every subsequent transfer.
Transactions in notes issued before April 01, 2027 must also comply with Paras 26 and 27.

rows: Only dematerialised form; minimum ₹1 crore at issuance and on transfers
May trade at amortised value even if ticket size falls below ₹1 crore
Size of investment by a single investor
Agreement with SPE must require arrangements with registrar, depository, stock exchange etc. to ensure compliance
Regulation 21 of SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008 to be complied with
Transactions in notes issued before April 01, 2027 must also comply with Paras 26 and 27

who_is_affected: All India Financial Institutions acting as originators, SPEs, and investors or intermediaries in securitisation notes.
action_required: Review securitisation structures and SPE agreements, and ensure demat arrangements and the ₹1 crore ticket-size controls are in place before April 01, 2027, including for existing notes.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 on November 23, 2026.

Key changes to the 2025 Directions, effective April 01, 2027:

• Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in dematerialised form.
• Minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore at issuance and at every subsequent transfer, with amortising notes allowed to trade at amortised value.
• Originators must ensure SPE agreements require arrangements with registrars, depositories and exchanges to ensure compliance.
• Public offers must comply with Regulation 21 of the SEBI securitised debt instruments regulations, 2008.
• Notes issued before April 01, 2027 are also covered for transactions after that date.

AIFIs and their advisers should review existing structures and documentation well ahead of the effective date.

Please verify the details with the official RBI notification (RBI/2026-27/307) before acting.
